neolux.name: NeoLux 1.3.0
neolux.changelog:
New water and wet weather: a sea without a visible pattern, puddles and
raindrop rings when it rains, clouds you can fly into and over, and enchanted
items that shimmer instead of turning into a purple sheet.

### Added

- Puddles: while it rains, water gathers in patches on open ground that faces
  the sky and mirrors its surroundings like a lake. They fill slowly as the
  rain goes on and dry up after it. `PUDDLES` and `PUDDLE_AMOUNT` on the World
  page.
- Raindrops ring standing water and puddles while it rains, `RAIN_RIPPLES` on
  the World page. Both are off in the Potato profile.
- Clouds sit at a fixed height in the world now, from Y=192 by default, and
  can be flown into and above. From inside they close in like fog, from above
  they cover the ground below. `CLOUD_HEIGHT` is a world height now rather
  than the distance above the player.
- Enchanted items, armor and dropped items have a program of their own for
  the glint and shimmer in the vanilla purple, by day and by night.
- `WATER_ROUGHNESS` on the Water page sets how choppy the surface is.

### Changed

- The water surface is built from three layers of noise instead of sine
  waves, so there is no regular pattern across a lake. The fine chop fades out
  with distance, and the far sea turns into a calm mirror.
- New water defaults: a calmer surface (roughness 0.25), higher waves, a
  stronger sun glint, more refraction and caustics, less underwater blur. The
  sliders reach further than these defaults in both directions.
- Underwater the view stays clear up close and turns deep blue with distance
  instead of grey. Red fades first, as it does in real water, and the blur
  starts six blocks away instead of at arm's length.
- Surfaces only get wet in biomes where it rains, not where it snows or
  stays dry.
- Cloud tops are brighter, so a cloud deck seen from above is white in the
  sun rather than beige.

### Fixed

- Black holes in the troughs of the waves. A steep wave mirrored the ground
  instead of the sky, and the screen space reflection followed that ray down
  to the sea bed.
- Speckled reflections on open water further than a few dozen blocks away,
  where the finest waves are smaller than a pixel.
- Enchanted items were covered by a flat purple sheet and lost their own
  color and lighting.

neolux.name: NeoLux 1.2.1
neolux.changelog:
Text on signs and the cracks on a block being mined show again.

### Fixed

- Sign text was invisible. Iris draws it with `gbuffers_block_translucent`,
  which the pack did not have, and the program it fell back to only fills the
  geometry buffers, after the lighting had already run. The pack ships that
  program now and lights the text itself.
- The cracks on a block being mined did not show. They were multiplied into
  the albedo after the deferred pass had lit the block, and go onto the
  finished color as well now.
- Dropped stained glass and translucent items in the hand found themselves in
  the colored shadow map and took their own color a second time, in blotches.
  They take shadow from opaque blocks only.

neolux.name: NeoLux 1.2.0
neolux.changelog:
Faster and cleaner: clouds at a quarter of their cost, cheaper shadows, FXAA,
light from a torch in the hand, and an end to the black rims that ran along
every edge against the sky.

### Added

- Light from the hand: a torch, lantern or any other light source held in
  either hand lights the surroundings and falls off one level per block, like
  the same block placed there. Faces turned away from the player get less of
  it. `HAND_LIGHT` on the Lighting page; turn it off when a dynamic lights mod
  does the same.
- FXAA on the tonemapped image, `FXAA` on the Post Processing page. On in
  every profile except Potato.
- Lightning has a program of its own and glows. It used to fall back to the
  entity program and was either never shaded or lit like a grey mob.
- The darkness a warden spreads dims every light and closes the view in to
  about fifteen blocks, as it does in vanilla.

### Changed

- Clouds read their value noise from the noise texture instead of hashing it,
  about four times faster: on a GTX 1070 Ti a screen full of sky at 8 steps
  takes 0.8 instead of 3.4 ms. The shapes are the same kind, in other places.
- The shadow filter looks at the centre and the outermost ring first and stops
  there when all of them agree, and reads the second shadow map and the tint
  only where they can matter. With colored shadows that is 1.8 to 2.4 times
  faster for filter 2 to 4. The light shafts skip the same lookups.
- Shadows keep their full strength over most of the shadow distance and fade
  out over the last part of the map. The fade used to start at the player,
  which left a shadow 80 blocks away at half strength.
- Water looks its shadow up once for the diffuse light and the sun glint.
- Tonemapping and grading moved from `final` to `composite3`. `final`
  sharpens the display ready image and keeps every pixel inside the range of
  its neighbours.
- Particles take the same block light falloff as the surfaces around them.
- With shadows and light shafts both off, the shadow pass is not rendered.

### Fixed

- Sharpening put a black rim on the dark side of every edge against the
  bright sky, and those rims crawled along leaves and fences as the camera
  moved.
- The star field was under twenty horizontal dashes near the horizon and
  nothing overhead. Stars are points about a pixel across now, several hundred
  of them, and they turn with the sky.
- Sugar cane, kelp, vines and the other stacked or hanging plants tore apart
  at every block seam in the wind. Each of their blocks moves as a whole now,
  and vines on a wall sway along it instead of into it. The upper half of a
  tall plant starts with the swing its lower half ends with.
- The lens flare shone through clouds.
- Powder snow fog was olive green.
- Entity faces jumped from lit to dark as they turned past the light.
- Banding in the dark night sky and in dusk gradients: the output is
  dithered.
- Twelve options showed their raw names in the menu: the whole cloud page,
  lens flare, mo

neolux.name: NeoLux 1.1.0
neolux.changelog:
A new look for the overworld: strong, warm sunlight against quiet shade, a sky
with a palette of its own, soft volumetric clouds and dark, mirroring water.

### Added

- Procedural volumetric clouds in place of the vanilla ones: a layer above the
  player, marched from base to top, lit towards the sun and shaded inside, so
  the puffs have a bright rim and a darker core. They show in water
  reflections too. `CLOUD_STYLE` switches between NeoLux, vanilla and none;
  the new Clouds page has cover, height, thickness, quality, speed and
  brightness.
- A soft tonemap (`TONEMAP` 4, the new default): linear through the midtones
  with a long shoulder, no toe, so shade keeps its detail.
- Lens flare along the line from the sun through the middle of the screen.
  `LENS_FLARE` on the Post Processing page.
- `SHADE_DESATURATION`: surfaces lit only by the sky lose part of their color
  and read grey next to the sunlit side.
- `MOON_BRIGHTNESS`, separate from the sun.
- Water gets fine ripples on top of the swell, which breaks up the reflection
  the way a real surface does.

### Changed

- The overworld sky, sunlight and ambient light run on their own palette that
  follows the height of the sun instead of the vanilla sky and fog colors. The
  vanilla fog color turns with the direction the camera faces, which tinted the
  whole sky differently whenever the player turned. The Nether and the End keep
  the vanilla driven colors.
- Sunlight is stronger and ambient light weaker, and block faces are shaded by
  their orientation, so shade has contrast and depth again.
- Fog is an aerial haze now: barely any on a clear day within the first hundred
  blocks, thicker at night and in rain, and brightest towards a low sun.
- Bloom trades part of each pixel for its blurred copy instead of being added
  on top, and with the threshold at zero every pixel takes part. That is the
  soft glow around bright surfaces; it no longer brightens the whole frame.
- Water is darker, drops the vanilla texture pattern and takes only the biome
  color, and reflects the full sky.
- The sun is bright enough to burn out and feed the bloom, tinted warm when it
  stands low.
- Shadow lookups are compared and filtered in hardware, so shadow edges ramp
  over the texels instead of stepping from one to the next.
- Defaults: `EXPOSURE` 1.00, `SATURATION` 1.00, `CONTRAST` 1.00,
  `VIGNETTE_STRENGTH` 0.35, `SKY_BRIGHTNESS` 1.00, `SUN_BRIGHTNESS` 8.00.

### Fixed

- The sun lit caves beyond the shadow distance: past the shadow map the lookup
  reports "lit", so direct light now also needs sky light to reach a surface.
- Half of every flower and grass tuft went black. A plant is two crossed quads
  and one of them always faces away from the sun; the shadow lookup was pushed
  along that back facing normal, away from the light and into the shade of the
  plant itself. Plants are now lit as if they faced straight up, like the
  ground they grow out of, take no normal offset in the shadow lookup but

## Yukee Shaders 0.8.2

A visual update focused on softer sky colors, responsive lighting, and more customization.

### Sky & Atmosphere
- Refreshed sky gradients with subtle pearlescent colors and rare daytime sparkles.
- Softer sunrise and sunset palettes featuring gold, peach, coral, and lilac tones.

brisa-lite.name: Brisa Lite 2.2
brisa-lite.changelog:
## Brisa Lite 2.2

- Added **depth-based water color and transparency**, with clearer shallows and darker deep water while preserving biome colors.
- Added **animated foam for currents and waterfalls**, separate from the existing shoreline foam.
- Added independent toggles and strength controls for both effects under **Water settings**. Ultra Lite keeps them disabled by default.
- Disabled **water refraction by default** in every preset. It can still be enabled manually.
- Removed **heat distortion** around lava and fire to reduce GPU overhead.
- Added richer **sunrise and sunset colors**, including orange and pink horizons, violet skies, and warmer clouds.
- Optimized block lighting, held-item lighting, material calculations, and stationary-camera motion blur.
- Preserved caustics, reflections, rain effects, shadows, bloom, and vegetation movement.
- Rechecked shader compilation across **31 supported Minecraft versions**, with in-game verification on **Minecraft 26.3 using Iris**.

The new water effects use the existing water rendering pass. Performance varies depending on hardware, settings, and scene.

# Brisa Lite 2.1

- Expanded verified Minecraft coverage to all stable releases in the 1.20 and 1.21 series, plus 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3.
- Added compatibility checks for Minecraft 1.16.5, 1.18.2 and the full 1.19 series through 1.19.4.
- Added version-aware copper torch and copper lantern mappings for Minecraft 1.21.9 and later.
- Fixed incorrect dark shadow bands on older Iris builds by using manual depth comparisons with the existing sampling count. Modern Iris keeps its original shadow path.
- Preserved the effects, visibility improvements, controls and performance presets from Brisa Lite 2.0.
- Included a detailed compatibility manifest with the Iris builds checked and the verification level for each Minecraft version.

All 31 listed versions passed official Iris compiler/transformer and native GPU
checks. Actual game sessions also passed on 1.20.1, 1.21.11 and all five listed
26.x releases. These tests used OpenGL; Vulkan and OptiFine were not verified.
Use Iris and Sodium builds that support your exact Minecraft version.

firmament-shaders.name: Firmament 0.3
firmament-shaders.changelog:
# Firmament 0.3

**Richer colour, calmer light.** Firmament no longer looks as if the brightness
were turned all the way up: colours stay saturated, daylight has contrast, and
nights, caves, the Nether and the End keep their mood.

- **New tone curve:** a hue-preserving filmic curve keeps mid-grey where it
  belongs. Sunlit sand and blossoms keep their colour instead of fading to
  white; only real highlights such as the sun roll off to white.
- **Juicier colour, not neon:** vibrance lifts sky, sand, blossoms and grass,
  while snow stays white and already vivid colours stay natural.
- **Eye adaptation:** centre-weighted metering, and dark scenes are no longer
  lifted to daylight brightness. Bloom only comes from truly bright light.
- **Sky:** a deep blue sky with a blue horizon, warm twilight bands, a sun halo,
  moon phases, twinkling stars and an optional Milky Way.
- **Morning mist:** low fog in valleys and over water at sunrise (optional).
- **Clouds:** white sunlit tops over grey bases.
- **Light:** torches and lanterns fall off naturally from golden to amber, and
  lava stays orange.
- **Nether and End:** relit. The Nether is dark and deep instead of a glowing red
  wall; the End island has shape instead of a flat white surface.
- **Rain** falls as grey streaks.
- **New settings:** Eye adaptation, Contrast, Vibrance, White balance, Vignette,
  Sharpening, Morning mist and Milky Way, in English and Russian.

The same 29 Minecraft Java versions as 0.22: **1.18.2**; **1.19, 1.19.1,
1.19.2 and 1.19.4**; **1.20–1.20.6**; **1.21–1.21.11**; **26.1, 26.1.1,
26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3**. The new gallery was rendered in Minecraft
**1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.228 / Iris 1.8.12 / Sodium 0.6.13** on the High preset.

Known: after reloading chunks with F3+A, shadows of blocks outside your view
appear once you look at them. Iris only builds chunks the camera sees.

Use the Iris and Sodium builds matching your Minecraft version; 26.2 and 26.3
target the OpenGL renderer. Keep the ZIP intact, place it in `shaderpacks`, and
select Firmament in Iris. Start with High and adjust the preset for your setup.

From 0.3 Firmament is licensed under the MDFL 1.0; 0.10 to 0.22 stay MIT.

A project by **PozziTiv4ik**.

firmament-shaders.name: Firmament 0.22
firmament-shaders.changelog:
# Firmament 0.22

**Faster clouds in rain and tidier shader code, with exactly the same picture.**

- **Clouds in rain:** about 1.05× faster. Cloud samples that are already fully
  dense skip noise that cannot change them; higher Cloud Coverage settings
  benefit too.
- **Under the hood:** repeated shader code now uses shared helpers, the
  reflection-snapshot pass decodes each pixel once, and unused declarations
  are gone.
- **Same image:** every automated comparison image is bit-identical to 0.21.
- **Nothing slower:** every other pass costs the same as in 0.21. Four
  further optimization ideas were measured and left out because they were not
  faster.

Timings are isolated GPU pass measurements against 0.21 on an RTX 4060 Laptop
GPU at 2560 × 1440 with the High preset, not frame rates. The sky, fog and
night-sky speed-ups of 0.21 are kept.

Rendering, presets, options and the 29 supported Minecraft Java versions are
unchanged from 0.21: **1.18.2**; **1.19, 1.19.1, 1.19.2 and 1.19.4**;

firmament-shaders.name: Firmament 0.21
firmament-shaders.changelog:
# Firmament 0.21

**A cleaner shader core and a faster sky, with the same look.**

- **Sky:** the atmosphere pass computes the sun and moon once per frame instead
  of once per pixel and is about 1.3× faster by day and night.
- **Fog and light shafts:** 1.06–1.17× faster above and below water.
- **Night sky:** stars and clouds over open sky about 1.06× faster; ambient
  occlusion reconstruction about 1.03×.
- **Under the hood:** shared shader code is reorganized, with named materials
  and one implementation of each lighting helper. Every other pass costs the
  same as in 0.2.

The figures are isolated GPU pass timings measured against 0.2 on an RTX 4060
Laptop GPU at 2560 × 1440 with the High preset, not frame rates. In-game FPS
depends on the scene, render distance and hardware.

firmament-shaders.name: Firmament 0.2
firmament-shaders.changelog:
# Firmament 0.2

**Performance release: more frames, the same look.**

- **Nether and End:** the unused sun shadow map is no longer rendered at all.
- **Overworld shadows:** a depth-only shadow pass; water and clear glass no
  longer reach the shadow rasterizer.
- **Cloud shadows:** read from a small map computed once per frame instead of
  several noise octaves per lit pixel. Sunlit surface lighting costs less than
  half as much as in 0.11.
- **Fog and light shafts:** cheaper shadow lookups along each ray (about 1.2×).
- **Sky:** clouds and stars are rendered after the terrain. Stars are drawn only
  where the sky is visible; in caves and sealed rooms, clouds hidden by terrain
  cost much less (about 2.4× for a cave view with a strip of sky).
- **Ambient occlusion:** open, unoccluded areas skip the reconstruction filter.

The figures are isolated GPU pass timings measured against 0.11 on an RTX 4060
Laptop GPU at 2560 × 1440 with the High preset, not frame rates. In-game FPS
depends on the scene, render distance and hardware.

lumenite-shaders.name: Lumenite Shaders 2.9.4
lumenite-shaders.changelog:
2.9.4: sun rays without the wash, steady clouds, whole feathers, real veils
- Sun Rays: the rays no longer add sun-coloured light over all open sky
  between the pixel and the sun, which washed out the screen when facing
  the sun. They now carve shadow beams where the path is blocked
  (lmn_rayShade) and add only a sixth of the old glow. Underwater shafts
  are unchanged. Shaft Glow's clear-sun baseline goes from 0.25 to 0.10.
  The lens flare was measured at about 1% of screen brightness, so it is
  not changed.
- Cloud map LOD: foot is now two map texels (0.0104), not eight
  (0.0406). The 128-block octave now holds to about 1350 blocks instead
  of fading between 300 and 800, so clouds stop growing and shrinking
  as you move.
- Billow/wisp LOD distances now scale with cloud resolution (2x at 100%).
- Slew limiter: the previous value is reprojected along the deck's wind,
  so drifting edges are no longer dragged.
- Cirrus feathers: existence and coverage are now taken at the feather's
  head, with a soft margin, instead of at each pixel. The early return
  is relaxed so feathers are not cut at the edge of a patch.
- Cumulus aerial perspective: the thin far part of a cloud now fades its
  opacity, so faded clouds no longer mask the sky detail behind them.
- Sky Detail veils rebuilt as combed fibrous sheets that fray into
  strands at their edges, replacing the Worley-torn patches.
- Changelog and lang updated. OPTIONS.md and the zip regenerated.

lumenite-shaders.name: Lumenite Shaders 2.9.3
lumenite-shaders.changelog:
A new sun and moon: the “Shader Sun and Moon” setting, now on by default. The sun has sunspots and turns red and flattens as it sets; the moon is a map of the real near side, with phases and earthshine. There are new Sun Size and Moon Size settings.
Bloom, rebuilt: the glow no longer races around when you move.
Fixes:
Turning toward the sun in caves no longer brightens the screen.
Clouds look right through gaps in leaves.
Vines, cave vines and weeping vines sway with the leaves.
Clouds no longer cut sun rays off completely.
Two small effects in the End now work: armour gem glints and roughness on distant water.
Defaults and settings: Cloud Resolution now offers 25% to 100%. “Clouds Break the Rays” is on in every preset except Potato.
Performance: bloom costs about the same as before, and the download is about 0.5 MB bigger for the moon map.

lumenite-shaders.name: Lumenite Shaders 2.9.1
lumenite-shaders.changelog:
Lumenite 2.9.1
Everything new since 2.8.4.
Clouds, rebuilt
New cloud style: Volumetric (realistic). It is the new default and is used in every preset. The previous realistic clouds are still there, unchanged, as Volumetric (classic).
Clouds that look like clouds. The new style is built from scratch. The rows of same-size puffy balls with fluffy loose ends are gone. Now:
Clouds come in every size, from big towers to small scraps. They crowd together in places and leave wide stretches of open sky in others, and sometimes line up in rows along the wind.
Each one has a flat grey base and a crisp, sunlit cauliflower top built of lobes on lobes, leaning downwind.
Edges only fray into torn wisps where a cloud is dying, and along the base when it rains.
Sunlight, done properly.
Sunlit faces are bright and shaded sides are grey, with real contrast between them. The skylight on the clouds used to be as bright as the sky itself, which washed out every shadow.
Clouds in front of the sun stand dark, with brilliant silver rims, instead of glowing white all over.
With the sun behind you, sunlit faces are at their brightest.
At golden hour, sunlit faces turn warm cream and gold over mauve shadows.
At sunset, the tops burn gold and rose over bases already in shadow. Higher clouds catch the light longest, so the altocumulus glow pink after the cumulus below have dimmed.
When the sun is low, clouds cast shadows on each other.
Clouds at different heights and sizes. Cloud bases are no longer one flat plane across the sky.
Bases are lower where the air is moister and higher on older, dying and spreading clouds, and they differ a little from cloud to cloud. From a hilltop you can see clouds at several levels at once.
Bases climb through the day as the ground heats up, and sink again at night.
Sizes vary: small, close-packed clouds in the morning, bigger and further apart by the afternoon, and some areas build big cloud masses while others stay a scatter of small ones.
Most clouds stay shallow and a few tower far above the rest.
The mid-level clouds sit at a different height every day, and rise and dip across the sky.
Clouds can now grow taller: the cloud layer reaches higher than before.
Clouds live and die. They form, grow and fade away while you watch, and a dying cloud frays apart.
The second cloud deck is now the mid-level sky. It used to be the same clouds again, higher up. Now it is altocumulus, rows of small rounded cloudlets, or a smooth grey altostratus veil the sun shows through as a pale disc. It drifts faster than the clouds below, and in a different direction.
Cirrus no longer draws thin bright arcs and rings across the sky. Its strands run along the wind.
Cirrocumulus is a soft rippled sheet instead of a field of hard white dots.
No more bright column in the clouds opposite a low sun.
Clouds no longer jump once an hour, when the game's timer wraps around.
Dynamic weather
The sky follows the day.

phero-visuals.changelog:
# Phero Visuals V3 — Balanced Lighting & Visual Enhancement Update

### ✨ What's New
- **Enhanced Minecraft Graphics:** Refined colors, balanced exposure, and subtle atmospheric improvements for a more beautiful vanilla-inspired experience.
- **Improved Sunlight Control:** Sun illuminance defaults to 92, with a shader-level limit of 99 to keep the configured value below 100.
- **Softer Bloom Effects:** Reduced excessive glow and sun halo for a cleaner, more natural appearance.
- **Refined Color Grading:** Slightly richer colors while preserving Minecraft's original visual identity.
- **Balanced Fog & Brightness:** Adjusted visual settings for a softer, less aggressive atmosphere.
- **Subtle Vignette:** Reduced screen-edge darkening for a cleaner overall image.

### 🛠️ Improvements
- Updated project version to **V3.0**.
- Refined shader settings for a balanced visual experience.
- Preserved the existing water shader source files.
- Reviewed shader include references and ZIP archive integrity.

### 🎮 Compatibility
- Targets Minecraft Java Edition **1.21.x** and newer version families.
- Requires a compatible shader loader, such as Iris Shaders or OptiFine.
- Compatibility with individual Minecraft releases and graphics configurations may vary and should be tested.

### 🌿 Design Philosophy
Phero Visuals focuses on subtle Minecraft shader enhancements rather than extreme realism. This release aims to improve lighting, color balance, and atmosphere while keeping the familiar vanilla Minecraft look.

**Discover a more beautiful Minecraft world with Phero Visuals V3 — balanced lighting, refined colors, and restrained visual effects.**
